text: A barrel has to hold its temperature within a few degrees, all shift long.
The barrel is split into heating zones, from the feed throat to the nozzle.
Each zone has heater bands clamped around it,
and a thermocouple: two different metals, joined at the tip.
Heat the joint, and it makes a tiny voltage that rises with temperature.
The controller compares it to the setpoint, and switches the heaters to hold it.
Most of the melting comes from the screw itself. The heaters keep each zone on target.
But bands burn out. A loose band can't pass its heat to the barrel, so it overheats and fails.
Terminals work loose, and wiring cooks.
And if a thermocouple backs out of its well, it reads low,
so the controller keeps heating, and the zone runs far too hot.
Warning signs: a zone that won't reach setpoint, output stuck at a hundred percent, or a zone that swings.
So: lock out and isolate the power first.
Check each band's resistance, or its current with a clamp meter.
Keep bands tight and terminals clean.
And make sure every thermocouple is fully seated.
